 Case management UNHCR’s integrated case management approach in Syria provides individualized and confidential support to children at risk, survivors of gender-based violence, and individuals experiencing mental health and psychosocial distress. Caseworkers follow a structured process that includes assessment, planning, referral, and follow-up, ensuring that interventions are tailored to each person’s needs and circumstances. Child protection case management focuses on engaging children and their caregivers in decisions that prioritize the child’s best interests, while GBV case management applies a survivor-centred approach that respects the survivor’s rights, choices, and dignity. MHPSS case management is embedded across health and protection sectors, offering multi-layered support that ranges from community-based psychosocial care to referrals for specialized mental health services. Together, these services promote safety, recovery, and resilience through coordinated, holistic support. Awareness-raising Awareness-raising is a key strategy in UNHCR’s protection programming, aimed at increasing knowledge, shifting harmful norms, and empowering communities to recognize and respond to protection risks. Child protection awareness sessions focus on children’s rights, the impact of violence and neglect, and the importance of education and positive parenting. GBV awareness activities promote gender equality, challenge discriminatory practices, and inform communities about available services and legal protection. MHPSS awareness efforts address stigma around mental health, promote emotional well-being, and provide practical guidance on managing stress, trauma, and other psychosocial challenges. These sessions are delivered in safe, accessible spaces and are designed to foster inclusive dialogue and community engagement. Explosive Ordnance Risk Education UNHCR, through its 12 partners, conducted explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) awareness sessions across 52 community centres in 14 governorates. These sessions aimed to sensitize communities to the dangers of unexploded ordnance, emphasizing three key safety messages: “Don’t Touch – Move Away – Report.” Participants received illustrated brochures with key messages provided by the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS), ensuring that these life-saving messages remain accessible after the sessions. The initiative reinforces the importance of avoiding hazardous items and reporting them promptly to prevent injuries and save lives. Community engagement UNHCR supports community-based structures that strengthen local capacity to protect and support vulnerable individuals. In child protection, structures such as children’s clubs and child welfare committees empower children and community members to identify risks, advocate for rights, and support peers. GBV programming engages women and men through dedicated committees that promote gender equality, raise awareness, and support survivors in accessing services and opportunities. MHPSS community engagement includes inclusive care programmes for older persons and persons with disabilities, as well as recreational and peer support activities that foster social cohesion and emotional resilience. These initiatives build trust, promote ownership, and ensure that protection responses are rooted in the lived realities of the communities they serve.

related.excerpt: What does a world leader do with a gun and six bullets? That was the conundrum Nato leaders faced after the Turkish president offered them each a revolver after the Ankara summit. Keir Starmer was the first to mention the highly unusual gift presented by Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to his guests. On the flight back from Ankara, where Nato leaders had gathered for two days, the British prime minister said he and others had received a revolver engraved with their names. Alongside the gun sitting in a red box lined in black were six live rounds and a note exempting the weapons from export controls. It was a surprising gift to say the least, several officials from the different alliance member states said, and gave rise to some “insane” scenes among the various delegations’ security teams. “An unusual gift from president Erdoğan at the Nato summit: a Magnum revolver with ammunition, engraved with my name,” the Hungarian prime minister, Péter Magyar, said on X. related.title: UK eyes $50 billion in pooled NATO funds for new long-range strike initiative
related.summary: VIENNA — The United Kingdom unveiled a $50 billion, decade-long push to accelerate European deep precision strike capabilities during the NATO summit on Wednesday, positioning London at the head of a coalition of twelve NATO allies. The British contribution to the sum is £3 billion ($4 billion), according to a press release by the prime minister’s office, which was split across a bilateral project with Germany and trilateral work with Italy and France on the Stratus missile.
bullets: VIENNA — The United Kingdom unveiled a $50 billion, decade-long push to accelerate European deep precision strike capabilities during the NATO summit on Wednesday, positioning London at the head of a coalition of twelve NATO allies.

The British contribution to the sum is £3 billion ($4 billion), according to a press release by the prime minister’s office, which was split across a bilateral project with Germany and trilateral work with Italy and France on the Stratus missile.

The new British announcement also sits against the broader backdrop of ELSA, the European Long-Range Strike Approach that France, Germany, Italy and Poland launched in July 2024, later joined by Sweden and the U.K.
The European scramble for deep-strike capabilities comes as the war in Ukraine has shown the devastating impact of these weapons on military supply lines far from the frontline.

The figure is less a single procurement contract than a financing and coordination structure meant to knit together a scattered set of national and bilateral missile programs that have been building since 2024.
related.excerpt: VIENNA — The United Kingdom unveiled a $50 billion, decade-long push to accelerate European deep precision strike capabilities during the NATO summit on Wednesday, positioning London at the head of a coalition of twelve NATO allies. The figure is less a single procurement contract than a financing and coordination structure meant to knit together a scattered set of national and bilateral missile programs that have been building since 2024. The announcement leans heavily on the idea of pooling, not building, new technology. British officials described the initiative as a mechanism to “share expertise, technology advances and deepen industrial collaboration to rapidly advance NATO capabilities,” rather than a specification for a single new weapon. The breadth of range requirements involved − everything from 300 kilometers to systems eventually exceeding 2,000 kilometers − spans engineering problems likely too disparate to be solved by a single missile design. Instead, the $50 billion appears to aggregate work already underway. related.title: Germany to buy US Tomahawks in shift toward own long-range capability
related.summary: Germany will purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles from the United States and station them on German soil, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday, in a shift from planned U.S. government on the sidelines of a NATO summit in Ankara, adding that the meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday had exceeded his expectations. “We are closing a critical strategic gap in our defence, while simultaneously working to develop our own European systems and station them in Europe,” he said.

related.excerpt: Germany will purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles from the United States and station them on German soil, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday, in a shift from planned U.S. deployments to Germany’s own long-range strike capability. Merz told lawmakers he had sealed the deal with the U.S. government on the sidelines of a NATO summit in Ankara, adding that the meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday had exceeded his expectations. “We are closing a critical strategic gap in our defence, while simultaneously working to develop our own European systems and station them in Europe,” he said. According to German government sources, Washington committed to granting approval in August for Germany to procure Tomahawk missiles and corresponding ground-based Typhon launchers in a letter of intent signed on Tuesday. The number of missiles and launchers Germany plans to acquire has not been disclosed as it is classified information. The planned purchase appears to fit with U.S. President Donald Trump’s push for European allies to pay for their own security, for example by buying U.S. weapons.
